sentimentIssues: AMD 'watch' at 517s is wrong; it is held and bullish.
RH '$120 to $200' reads as a target band; it should be 'from ~120 to 200'.
19 sentiment rows for 9 names (AMD x5, AXP x3, RH x4); duplicates with alternating hold/long for AMD.
The TSM neutral row is correct and useful context. GSG 'bearish' is correct.
why: Ours captures every actionable position with sizes: WYNN $8,400, CELH $11,000, NKE ~$35, RH ~$170k -> $250-400k. It also keeps the AMD $700 correctly as a do-not-sell threshold and covers the Fed, inflation and commodities risk section. LeapEdge omits two real purchases (NKE, CELH) as trade ideas, turns the AMD $700 trim threshold into a target, adds 'AI' and misses the whole macro-risk half. Ours still pays the usual tax: WYNN/AXP/NKE/CELH have null tickers, calls and sentiment rows are duplicated, and 16 omission lines are pipeline noise.
recommendations: Add a 'position size / executed today' field to calls. 'Bought $8,400 WYNN', 'bought $11,000 CELH' and 'RH +$20k today, ~$170k total, building to $250-400k' are what a PM wants first.
Separate 'price target' from 'trim/no-sell threshold' in the schema. Ours got AMD right; make it structural so it stays right.
Resolve company names to tickers ('win resorts'/'Winning Resorts' -> WYNN, American Express -> AXP, Nike -> NKE, Celsius -> CELH). Never null a literal ticker like 'AMD'.
Mark conditional views explicitly ('AXP 400+ IF oil/rates peak'; 'RH 120->200 IF oil peaks') and keep ranges' from/to semantics. Ours wrote 'toward $120 to $200'.
Identify quoted guests when named on air (Gundlach, Fed chair Warsh). Do not write 'speaker identities unknown' when the transcript names them.
Collapse the two WYNN calls and the two RH calls into one call each, holding near-term trigger, long-term target and size.
